title: Accounts docs
intro: Accounts is the sign-up and sign-in system of your own website and admin: one user list for your shoppers and your staff, with roles. Visitors sign in with the widget or with your own screens on the API; your server and our other products check their sign-ins offline with your website's public keys. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so the accounts made there are real. There is no test mode.
methods: Sign-in methods are features: Phone code (a code by SMS or WhatsApp), Phone + password, Email + password, Email code / magic link, Google, Apple and Facebook. Turn on the ones you want; the widget shows exactly those. Phone code and Phone + password share the phone format (default calling code and trunk prefix, Settings → Phone numbers; an empty calling code means your business.json country's): numbers are kept as E.164, the way every product reads them, so +44 07700 900123, 0044 7700 900123, 447700900123 and 07700-900123 (with +44) are one number. Codes, magic links, password resets and invites are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections and write these templates in Notifications (keys below, with the values each one gets). Phone + password's Forgot password sends accounts.phone_code on the Phone code channel; with Forgot password off, its link opens your own page (for example a WhatsApp chat). Without Notifications, those steps answer notifications_not_connected, except Forgot password: both Forgot password routes answer 202 at once whether or not the address has an account and whatever the send gives (a cooldown or cap sends nothing), and a reset link or code Notifications cannot send now is sent again right after later requests while it is valid. Reset links open the returnTo page on your website's domain, or on one of your hosts listed in resetHosts (for example your admin's own host, over https). Forgot password by email takes resetLimit requests per address per 15 minutes (default 3; 1 to 20), counted for every address whether or not it has an account; more answer 429 rate_limited. Email codes wait 30 seconds between sends and stop at 6 per address each hour (too_soon). Phone codes last codeMinutes (default 10), wait between sends (cooldownSeconds, refusal code_cooldown with retryAt), are capped per number and per website each hour (code_limit), may be limited to your countries (country_not_allowed), and a new user without a name gets the newUserName template ({last4}: the number's last 4 digits). An email code, a magic link or a Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in opens only an account whose email address was proven (by an earlier code or link, a password reset, an invite, a social sign-in or staff entering it); an address typed but never proven (at a phone sign-up, in a role request or at an email + password sign-up) counts as unknown, so the sign-up that follows answers already_exists and that account is never opened. Forgot password by email sends its link only to a proven address or to the address the account was made with (an email + password sign-up, an email invite): for an address only typed on an account that signs in another way, it answers 202 as for an unknown address and sends nothing. A sign-in code from staff typed in the email code screen opens its user but proves no address.
social: Google, Apple and Facebook use your own app keys (Connections). Register the return address below with the provider. The widget opens the provider's page; the provider sends the person back to Accounts, which finds or creates the user and returns the browser to your page with a single-use code in the address fragment; the widget exchanges it for the sign-in.
signIns: A sign-in is a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519) that lasts 15 minutes: iss is Accounts' address, aud is your website id, sub is the user id, and it carries name, email with email_verified, phone with phone_verified and, with Roles and permissions on, role and permissions (* = every permission). The widget renews it with the user's session (session length and remember me are set per role; defaults 1 day and 30 days). Verify it on your server with the public keys (no call per check), and paste the Accounts server token into other products so they trust sign-ins too. A sign-in only says who the user is: it never authorizes admin actions in any product — those need your server token or a ticket.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own screens on the visitor API with the browser token. Routes of a signed-in user also take the sign-in in the SS-Sign-In header. Sign-in and sign-up routes answer { status: signed_in, signIn, expiresAt, refreshToken, sessionExpiresAt, remember, user }, { status: two_step, challenge, expiresAt }, { status: two_step_setup, challenge, expiresAt, secret, otpauthUrl } or { status: pending }; the API reference below gives every route's body and answer. Keep the refresh token in the browser and renew with POST /v1/session/refresh: each renew answers a new refresh token; the old one presented again within 30 seconds (parallel requests, a retried renew) gets the same new pair, and later it ends the session (it was copied).
roles: One user list: every new sign-up gets the Customer role; GET /v1/users/count and /v1/users/counts?by=status|role count it with the list's filters (q, role, roles, permission, status, blocked, deletion, phone, phoneDigits, createdAfter). The ready-made roles (Owner, Business manager, Product manager, Marketing manager, Support staff) start with default permissions from Accounts, Chat, Notifications and Ecommerce (Owner has every permission), can be changed and copied, and you can add your own. A role's permissions come from the products whose server tokens you pasted into Accounts (each product publishes its list), plus your own permission names (site:<name>). A role also sets two-step (optional or required), the session length and remember me, and: rank (a smaller number ranks higher: Owner 100, Business manager 200, Product manager 300, Marketing manager 400, Support staff 500, Customer 900; your own roles sit between 101 and 899), remember (ask, ask_ticked, always: no box, always remembered, or never: no box, never remembered, so the session ends when the browser closes and, on the server, at the latest after the longer of the session length and the remember-me days; a sign-in answers remember: false, so the widget keeps the session in sessionStorage and your server keeps it in a cookie without an expiry), methods (the sign-in methods its users may use; [] = all; others get method_refused), signIn (on, or paused: its users, and new sign-ups while Customer is paused, get sign_in_paused with your paused text, before any code is sent), logSignIns (sign-ins, failures with their IP, resets, recovery-code use and new recovery codes go to the activity log) and sessionRolling (false: a session ends at a fixed time after sign-in; true: each renewal moves its end to the session length, or the remember-me days, from then, so a session in use does not end). Your admin checks the user's role and permissions before it asks a product for a ticket.
rules: Sign-up rules (Approval / invite sign-up): open sign-up, invite only, or approval required, and which standard fields are required. Custom fields (text, number, date, choice) are set in the dashboard. Profile settings (shown while any sign-in method is on): addresses per user (up to 10), keep at least one address, and the required address fields; addresses have a label (for example Home or Office), an area and one default address. Security: password rules (a minimum length up to 128, a maximum length of 128 to 256 (default 256), at least one letter and one digit (off by default), the breached-password check, and the personal check that refuses the name, the email's local part or runs like 1234 or qwer; a refused password answers weak_password with the rule it breaks: too_short with minLength, too_long with maxLength, letter_and_digit, personal or breached), a fixed or growing lock after repeated wrong passwords, two-step codes or recovery codes (growing: 1 minute, doubling up to 60; two-step is refused while the lock lasts), a limit of tries per network and address per 15 minutes (the right password clears them), two-step sign-in with recovery codes (a signed-in user replaces them with POST /v1/me/two-step/recovery-codes { code } or { recoveryCode }: a code from the app or one recovery code proves the step, the old codes stop working, wrong codes count toward the lock; My account has New recovery codes), risk checks against disposable email addresses and many accounts from one device or network, and terms acceptance (the version each user accepted is kept).
dataRights: Download my data gives the user one single-use link (15 minutes) to everything Accounts and every product whose token you pasted keep about them. Delete my account waits for your approval in the Users admin widget (or for the days set in Settings), then erases the user here and in every connected product; a product that cannot be reached is asked again on later requests.
activity: Activity log copy: paste this website's Accounts server token into your other products; each one then sends every staff action to Accounts: who (with the acting user's role), what, the target and its label (for example an order number), a short detail and when — never message contents, secrets or addresses. Read the copies with GET /v1/activity-copies?productId=&actor=&action=&target=&q=&from=&to= (newest first; action takes one action or several separated by commas, q searches labels, details, names and targets, from and to take an ISO-8601 time or a day in your business.json time zone) and count them with GET /v1/activity-copies/count and /v1/activity-copies/counts?by=productId|action|actor. Accounts' own log (users and roles, with each user's name or role as the label) is read with GET /v1/activity.
orders: Orders tab: paste the Ecommerce server token; My account then lists the user's last 20 orders from Ecommerce (GET /v1/customers/<userId>/orders on Ecommerce, with the server token you pasted): number, status (the status label your shop set) and total.
staff: Staff and customers from your server: POST /v1/users creates an active user { name, email?, phone?, role?, password?, addresses?, notes?, custom? } and sends nothing (an email address or a phone number is needed); PATCH /v1/users/:id also changes email and phone (normalized, unique, marked verified; null removes one), password (the user is signed out everywhere), addresses and twoStep: false (turns another user's two-step sign-in off, for example when its secret can no longer be read; they set it up again); DELETE /v1/users/:id { reason } erases the user at once here and in every connected product; DELETE /v1/users/:id?scope=accounts removes them from Accounts only (the user, their sessions and codes) and every other product keeps its data: use it to remove someone from your team. Add user and invites make an account that signs in by its email address when it has one, else by its phone number (Forgot password by email follows it). Answers carry hasPassword, roleSince, lockedUntil and recoveryCodesLeft. GET /v1/users?permission=<product>:<key>&blocked=false lists the unblocked users whose role grants a permission (products' staff alerts read it). Guards, always, when the call names the acting user (SS-Actor-Id, the Accounts user id) or comes with a ticket: nobody changes their own role, blocks or deletes themselves; nobody edits, blocks or deletes a user whose role ranks above theirs, or gives a role ranking above theirs; the last unblocked Owner is never demoted, blocked or deleted (403 forbidden). Without an acting user your server token stays all-powerful.
serverSignIn: Sign-in from your server: every sign-in, sign-up, code, renew and sign-out route also takes your server token with the visitor's address in SS-Visitor-IP (required on writes; it drives the per-visitor limits and the risk checks) and, optionally, the visitor's browser in SS-Visitor-Agent (the device list names it). The answer carries the refresh token in the body for your server to keep; renew with POST /v1/session/refresh. Routes of a signed-in user take the sign-in in SS-Sign-In as usual.
imported: Passwords from another system (importers): bcrypt hashes ($2a$, $2b$, $2y$, any cost) and PBKDF2 hashes written as pbkdf2$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash> (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of <pepper>:<password>, base64) sign in as they are; paste that system's pepper into Connections → Pepper of imported passwords. After the first good sign-in the password is saved the Accounts way. Imported two-step sign-in keeps its authenticator secret, and its old recovery codes (sha256 of recovery: and the code) each work once.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widgets where they should appear: sign_in, my_account, and role_request (Role requests: visitors ask for a role, for example membership). The sign-in widget also takes setup links (?ss_setup=<code> on its page). Widgets render nothing while their features are off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket. Users (users.read to see, users.manage to change): status chips with their counts, search and filters, each user's detail, Add user, Edit (contacts, password, notes, custom fields, addresses), Invite (sent, or the link handed to you), and in its More menu a sign-in code and a setup link (Staff sign-in codes and setup links), sign out everywhere, approve or decline a sign-up, keep or delete on a deletion request, block, and Delete user behind a typed confirmation (or remove them from Accounts only, keeping their data in your other products); with Role requests on, the requests list with invite, decline and open again. Roles (roles.manage). Activity (activity.read, Activity log copy): every product's copies with counts per product and filters. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Routes answer JSON, or nothing where the reference shows no answer (204, and 202 for Forgot password); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code (a refused field is named in errors[0].path), and our widgets show your own texts for them, never the English detail. The users, role requests and activity copies are paged with cursor and limit, newest first. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. The reference below gives each route's body, query parameters and answer; our tests check every answer against it.

phone_password: Routes: POST /v1/sign-up/phone-password, POST /v1/sign-in/phone-password { phone, password, remember }, POST /v1/password/phone/forgot { phone } and POST /v1/password/phone/reset { phone, code, password }. PUT /v1/me/password also serves users with a phone number. Settings: visitors can sign up (off: only you give passwords, through Add user, setup links and invites; sign-up answers sign_up_closed), minimum length (6–128), maximum length (128–256), letter and digit, breached-password check, wrong passwords before a lock, the lock, Forgot password (code or off) and the Forgot password page.
staff_links: POST /v1/users/:id/sign-in-code answers { code, expiresAt }: 6 digits for staff to read to the user, never sent, single use, typed into the phone-code, email-code or phone + password screen; a new one cancels the old. POST /v1/users/:id/setup-link answers { url, expiresAt }: it lets the user choose a password (also without an email address) through POST /v1/setup-links/accept { code, password }, which signs them in; using the link proves the user's phone number (you send the link to it, so their guest orders and points join the account) and signs their other devices out. Set your setup page with {code} (for example https://shop.com/account/setup/{code}); without one the link opens your website with ?ss_setup=, which the sign-in widget takes. POST /v1/users/invite takes deliver: return to answer the invite link instead of sending it. Each is logged with the acting user.
role_requests: Visitors ask with POST /v1/role-requests { role, name, phone | email, note } (no account; the roles you list in Settings). Your server and the Users widget read GET /v1/role-requests?status=pending|invited|completed|declined|expired (with counts), and POST /v1/role-requests/:id/invite (creates the user, or gives the role to the user with that phone or email, and answers a setup link unless they already have a password; a user who never proved that phone or email gets nothing and the invite answers 409 contact_unverified until you check with the person, confirm it on their user or remove that account), /decline and /reopen. A request is completed when the password is set or the role given; expired when its setup link ran out. Users carry roleSince (Member since).
import: Moving in from another system (ss-import, server token): POST /v1/import/roles, /fields, /users, /requests and /copies take NDJSON of Accounts' own record shapes with their ids, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB a call (?dryRun=1 checks without writing and reports every refused line; a record replaces the stored one with its key, and an unknown field, websiteId too, refuses it by name); /v1/import/:collection/prune removes records an import wrote that the source no longer has (never records made in Accounts itself); POST /v1/import/finish and GET /v1/import/status (counts and sums). Import roles first: a user's role must exist. A user's roleSince defaults to its createdAt; a user or request without createdAt keeps the one stored, else gets the time of the import. Users keep their password hashes (bcrypt, pbkdf2$ with the Pepper of imported passwords connection, scrypt$) and their two-step secrets, sealed at once; an email address or phone number another user holds is refused. Nothing is sent. Switch the feature off once the import is verified.
